name: Switch, Inc.
founded: 2000 (Las Vegas, NV, by Rob Roy; NYSE-listed October 2017; taken private December 2022)
ownership: private (DigitalBridge-managed, with IFM Investors; Aware Super minority stake since July 2023; confidential US IPO filing reported by Bloomberg, August 2026)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Switch is the patent-moated, Tier 5-branded US colocation landlord racing back to the public markets: it filed confidentially for a US IPO in August 2026 (per Bloomberg) after hiring banks for a listing that could raise up to $10B and value it at up to $80B including debt as soon as Q4 2026 (per Reuters, July 2026; Bloomberg's July report put the target near $50B) — less than four years after DigitalBridge and IFM Investors took it private for ~$11B — carrying more than $24B raised since 2024, a 12GW non-binding Oklo nuclear master agreement, and Rob Roy's EVO AI Factories rated to 2MW per rack into the AI buildout. An Andreessen Horowitz-led private round targeting about $2B, with Ben Horowitz expected to join the board, was reported alongside the filing. BACKGROUND: Founded 2000 in Las Vegas by Rob Roy — still founder, CEO and designer of record (950+ issued and pending patent claims per the company). Six announced US campus locations: The Core (Las Vegas, up to 495MW at completion), The Citadel (Tahoe Reno — opened 2017 with a claim as the largest data-center campus in the world, planned to 17.4M sq ft and marketed at gigawatts of power at completion), The Pyramid (Grand Rapids, up to 1.8M sq ft / 320MW), The Keep (Atlanta, up to ~150MW, plus a $772M 'Keep 2.0' campus in Cartersville, GA), a Texas ecosystem (The Rock in Round Rock on land bought from Dell, plus Data Foundry's Austin/Houston sites — over 2M sq ft and 185MW announced) and a 382-acre Beaver County, Pennsylvania campus announced April 2026; 300+ acres more are banked at Apex Industrial Park, North Las Vegas (~$180M across two 2025-26 purchases, per Las Vegas Review-Journal/DCD). All facilities 100% renewable-powered since January 2016 with net-zero Scope 1-2 emissions, per company statements. NYSE-listed 2017-2022; final public-year guidance was $660-674M revenue and $345-357M adjusted EBITDA (FY2022); no revenue or EBITDA has been disclosed since the take-private. Customers per Reuters include NVIDIA, Dell Technologies and FedEx; CoreWeave ran the world-first NVIDIA GB200 (Nov 2024) and GB300 NVL72 (Jul 2025) bring-ups inside Switch AI Factories.
ecosystemRole: We assess Switch as the design-led counterweight to the pure wholesale giants: the only US operator-landlord at this scale that productized its own facility standard (Tier 5 Platinum), holds its differentiation in a founder-authored patent estate rather than land position alone, and sells retail colocation, wholesale capacity and a packaged AI-factory product from the same campuses. Basis: company releases and trade coverage — world-first GB200/GB300 deployments landed in its EVO AI Factories; a $1.9B Schneider Electric supply-capacity agreement industrializes the 2MW-per-rack design; and its self-attributed position as the largest single data-center ABS issuer since 2024 ($4.2B across five issuances, plus the largest green data-center CMBS at $2.4B) gives it a securitization franchise second only to Vantage's in this cohort. For power-chain vendors it is a standards-driven, Nevada-anchored buyer that self-funds power infrastructure — a first-of-kind $2.6B (now $3.5B) syndicated performance letter-of-credit facility backs its transmission and generation commitments — and signs decade-scale offtakes (Oklo 12GW through 2044, Ormat 20-year geothermal).

productsAndServices.name: Exascale Prime campuses — retail and wholesale colocation (core business)
productsAndServices.description: Build-own-operate colocation across giant single-market campuses the company brands 'Prime' locations, each anchoring a US latency zone: The Core (Las Vegas — southwestern zone, up to 495MW at completion, 5ms to Los Angeles), The Citadel (Tahoe Reno — northwestern zone, planned to 17.4M sq ft, marketed at gigawatts of power at completion, 4.5ms to the Bay Area), The Pyramid (Grand Rapids — northeastern zone, up to 1.8M sq ft / 320MW, anchored by the adaptive reuse of the Steelcase pyramid), The Keep (Atlanta — southeastern zone, up to ~150MW, plus the $772M Keep 2.0 campus in Cartersville, GA, first phase cited for Q2 2026), and the Texas ecosystem (The Rock, Round Rock, on 1.5M+ sq ft of land bought from Dell next to Dell's HQ, plus Data Foundry's Austin/Houston facilities — over 2M sq ft and 185MW announced). A sixth campus on 382 acres in Beaver County, Pennsylvania (greater Pittsburgh) was announced April 2026 for East Coast finance/healthcare/government latency. Unlike most wholesale peers, Switch retains a large multi-tenant retail base: the securitized trust alone serves 550+ customers, ~84% of trust revenue from investment-grade tenants (per DBRS-rated ABS disclosures, April 2026).
highlights: Five operating campus ecosystems plus Pennsylvania announced — all Tier 5 Platinum-designed, 100% renewable-powered since January 2016
The Citadel opened 2017 with the company's claim as the largest, most advanced data-center campus in the world
300+ acres banked at Apex Industrial Park, North Las Vegas (~$180M, Dec 2025-2026 purchases) for future Nevada growth
Customers per Reuters include NVIDIA, Dell Technologies and FedEx; CoreWeave is the marquee AI tenant
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Vantage/Aligned/QTS-style pure wholesale developers, Switch sells a standards-and-density story (Tier 5 Platinum, 2MW per rack) rather than raw build-to-suit scale; against retail incumbents Equinix and Digital Realty it wins on campus power depth and single-operator design control. Its five-zone US footprint is a deliberate latency lattice — every campus pitched as covering a quadrant of the country — rather than a metro-by-metro land bank.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct colocation contracts (retail cabinets to multi-hall wholesale) plus long-term single-tenant leases; capacity is financed through ABS/CMBS against in-place leases.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers and AI clouds (CoreWeave, and per Reuters NVIDIA and Dell as customers)
Large enterprises (FedEx-class) needing US multi-site colocation
Government, finance, healthcare and education (stated target of the Pennsylvania campus)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Keep 2.0 Cartersville first phase cited Q2 2026 (per Bartow County filings); Beaver County, PA campus in pre-development (no announced timeline); Apex/North Las Vegas land held for future capacity; EVO AI Factory construction underway across all five campuses per the July 2025 release.

productsAndServices.name: EVO AI Factories (Rob Roy's AI-factory product)
productsAndServices.description: Switch's productized AI data center: a hybrid air-and-liquid-cooled hall design rated for rack densities from 20kW up to 2MW per rack ('100X'), with five separate fluidic system pathways delivering liquid-to-air and liquid-to-chip cooling at independently controlled pressures and temperatures into an enclosed 'EVO Chamber' (patent pending, US Serial No. 19/213,614). Aligned to NVIDIA DGX/MGX roadmaps from Blackwell through Rubin; hosted the industry-first NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 bring-up (CoreWeave, November 2024) and the world-first GB300 NVL72 bring-up (CoreWeave on Dell rack-scale systems, July 2025). Operated by 'LDC EVO', Switch's living-data-center operating system that replaces conventional DCIM with a physics-accurate digital twin built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and OpenUSD (integrated with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, announced March 2026, with partners including Dell, Schneider Electric, Cadence, ETAP, Dassault Systèmes, Oxide and Procore).
highlights: Construction underway across all five campuses including Tahoe Reno and Atlanta (company release, July 2025)
$1.9B two-phase Schneider Electric supply-capacity agreement (November 2025) locks prefabricated power modules and Uniflair chillers for the rollout
Two consecutive 'world-first' NVIDIA platform bring-ups are the product's proof points
Showcased in the DSX AI Infrastructure Pavilion at NVIDIA GTC 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Versus Vantage/Aligned AI halls (250kW-class liquid-cooled designs) Switch markets an order-of-magnitude higher density ceiling (2MW per rack) and a facility operating system, not just a shell — the pitch is a co-engineered NVIDIA-generation-cadence product. The 2MW figure is a design rating, not a disclosed operating density; treat competitive comparisons accordingly.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Colocation/lease agreements within existing Switch campuses; supply chain locked through OEM agreements (Schneider) rather than self-manufacture.
targetSegments: Neoclouds and AI platforms (CoreWeave is the named tenant)
Enterprises adopting NVIDIA reference AI factories
productsAndServices.roadmap: Phased EVO capacity deliveries across all five campuses (no per-site MW disclosed); design track follows NVIDIA Blackwell-to-Rubin cadence; LDC EVO/Omniverse DSX operational rollout from March 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Tier 5 Platinum standard and the patent portfolio (productized design moat)
productsAndServices.description: Switch wrote its own facility standard — Tier 5 Platinum — and built the brand into every campus. Beyond Tier IV-style redundancy it specifies 30+ additional elements, per the company: 100-hour fault-tolerant standby power (vs 12 hours at Tier IV), indefinite cooling operation without water, all cooling water kept outside the building shell, zero roof penetrations with dual independently replaceable roofs, 10 on-net carriers with 6 entry vaults on 2+ pathways, per-rack physical security, 100-hour shelter-in-place, mandatory 100% renewable power from new local projects, and a trailing-average PUE below 1.3. The standard is self-declared (not an Uptime Institute rating) and doubles as the spec sheet for Rob Roy's patent estate — 950+ issued and pending patent claims (company figure, 2026; 700+ cited by DigitalBridge in 2023) covering T-SCIF heat-containment rows, the TSC multi-mode exterior cooling units, POWER SPINE distribution and Switch SHIELD dual-roof systems.
highlights: Tier 5 Platinum branding applied to every campus and carried into MOD build-to-suit sales
Patented designs are OEM-manufactured — the company states 80% of what goes into a Switch MOD facility is OEM-built
The standard hardwires sustainability (renewables, PUE) into a resiliency rating — unusual among facility standards
productsAndServices.positioning: No direct competitor claims a 'Tier 5'; the label competes with Uptime Tier IV certifications held by peers. The moat is asserted through patents and marketing rather than third-party certification — a differentiation strategy that trades auditability for brand control.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Embedded in colocation pricing and MOD licensing/build-to-suit contracts; not sold as a standalone certification.
targetSegments: Mission-critical enterprises and public sector (resiliency buyers)
AI tenants needing density plus uptime guarantees
productsAndServices.roadmap: EVO Chamber patent (filed 2025, pending) extends the estate into AI-factory cooling; no announced plan to seek third-party certification of Tier 5.

productsAndServices.name: Switch MOD — build-to-suit and modular data centers
productsAndServices.description: Single-tenant facilities built to Switch's patented designs in three form factors: MOD 250 (PRIME) — a 250-foot-wide exascale building scalable to any length, built to Tier 5 Platinum; MOD 100 (REGIONAL EDGE) — a 100-foot-wide single-user facility deployable on parcels as small as 400x400 feet; and MOD 15 (EDGE) — an air-transportable edge unit housing 24-100+ cabinets. The company claims MOD 250/100 deliver Tier 5 Platinum resiliency at costs comparable to competitors' Tier 2/3 builds, on the strength of OEM-manufacturing 80% of facility content.
highlights: Extends the patented design system beyond Switch's own campuses to customer sites
Modular manufacturing is the cost/speed argument — standardized, pretested layouts
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with build-to-suit programs at Vantage, Aligned and STACK and with modular vendors; differentiated by the Tier 5 spec and patent estate rather than balance-sheet scale.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Build-to-suit development agreements bundled with Switch CONNECT telecom services.
targetSegments: Enterprises and agencies wanting dedicated facilities
productsAndServices.roadmap: No publicly announced MOD pipeline; offering maintained on the current product page.

productsAndServices.name: Switch CONNECT and The CORE Cooperative (telecom services)
productsAndServices.description: Carrier-neutral connectivity plus a telecom buying cooperative: Switch CONNECT audits customer telecom spend and resells carrier services purchased at the aggregate buying power of the combined customer base (The CORE Cooperative, developed under Chief Connectivity Officer Chris Donnelly), with claimed savings of 35-60%. Physical backbone is the Switch SUPERLOOP — a private fiber loop linking the Nevada campuses to California markets at 7ms Las Vegas-Reno and 4.5ms Citadel-Bay Area, letting tenants serve California workloads from cheaper, lower-risk Nevada real estate. Tier 5 spec guarantees 10 on-net carriers per facility.
highlights: SUPERLOOP converts Nevada geography into a California latency product
Telecom cooperative is a stickiness/TCO lever layered onto colocation contracts
productsAndServices.positioning: Not an interconnection ecosystem play like Equinix — the pitch is cost reduction and California-adjacent latency, not network density; carrier neutrality plus cooperative pricing against carrier-owned colocation.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with colocation agreements; audit-led sales motion.
targetSegments: Multi-site enterprises with large telecom spend
productsAndServices.roadmap: No announced expansions; SUPERLOOP capacity grows with campus buildouts.

productsAndServices.name: Power procurement and sustainability platform
productsAndServices.description: Switch buys and finances its own power position rather than building generation: 100% renewable supply across all campuses since January 1, 2016 (via PPAs and renewable credits, with net-zero Scope 1-2 claimed), a non-binding 12GW master power agreement with Oklo (December 2024) to be drawn down through individual PPAs on Aurora fast-reactor powerhouses through 2044, and a 20-year, ~13MW geothermal PPA with Ormat from the Salt Wells plant near Fallon, NV (January 2026; deliveries from Q1 2030, with a ~7MW solar add option) — Ormat's first direct data-center PPA. The financing arm is part of the product: an industry-first $2.6B syndicated performance letter-of-credit facility (April 2026, upsized to $3.5B by June 2026) exists specifically to back utility performance-assurance obligations for new transmission and generation, and the company publicly committed to self-funding its power infrastructure in Texas (Abbott data-center standards) and Pennsylvania.
highlights: Oklo 12GW is among the largest corporate clean-power agreements ever signed — but non-binding, with no operating Oklo plant yet (first Aurora targeted late 2027 at Idaho National Laboratory per trade press)
Water: 'net positive' commitment — replenish up to 2x operational use over the coming decade; zero-water closed-loop cooling and recycled-effluent pipeline projects in host communities
Publicly aligned with ratepayer-protection politics: backs Governor Abbott's Texas standards (August 2026) — pay-your-own-way as market positioning
productsAndServices.positioning: Contrast with Vantage (gas microgrids via VoltaGrid/Liberty) and Crusoe (owned generation): Switch stays a creditworthy offtaker — using LC capacity, long-dated PPAs and nuclear options instead of putting turbines on its balance sheet.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility tariffs and PPAs backed by the syndicated LC facility; renewable attributes passed through to tenant ESG reporting.
targetSegments: Its own campuses (grid-constrained Nevada, Georgia, Texas, Pennsylvania markets)
Tenants buying 100%-renewable colocation for Scope 3 claims
productsAndServices.roadmap: Oklo PPAs to be individually bound as project milestones hit (through 2044); Ormat deliveries Q1 2030; LC facility expected to upsize further, per EVP Jon Edwards (April 2026).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Switch is executing a deliberately sequenced return to public markets at the AI cycle's peak. Basis: a confidential S-1 filed roughly 44 months after the $11B take-private (Bloomberg, Aug 2026), five bulge-bracket banks on an up-to-$10B raise at a press-reported $50–80B including debt, and an a16z-led ~$2B private round with a Ben Horowitz board seat expected — equity events stacked around the EVO AI-factory narrative.

(High confidence) We assess the self-authored Tier 5 standard plus the patent estate functions as a genuine engineering moat fused to marketing — and that reference deployments, not certifications, are its proof. Basis: 950+ issued and pending patent claims (T-SCIF, POWER SPINE, Switch SHIELD, the pending EVO Chamber), Tier 5's 100-hour standby and waterless-cooling requirements (explicitly not an Uptime Institute rating), and two consecutive world-first NVIDIA bring-ups — GB200 (Nov 2024) and GB300 NVL72 (Jul 2025) — executed by CoreWeave and Dell inside Switch halls.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Switch's power posture is offtaker, not owner — contracted clean firm power over behind-the-meter generation. Basis: the 12GW non-binding Oklo master agreement through 2044 (no operating plant yet — execution risk is real), a 20-year Ormat geothermal PPA with deliveries from 2030, 100% renewable procurement since 2016, and an industry-first $3.5B syndicated performance-LC facility that collateralizes utility transmission and generation commitments — the structural opposite of Vantage's microgrid-ownership path.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the financing machine was deliberately rebuilt for development velocity ahead of the listing. Basis: 100% of the $6.5B take-private bank debt retired through securitization by July 2025, the October 2025 ABS dedicated purely to new development, roughly $24B raised since 2024 across five green ABS and the largest green data-center CMBS on record, and a $1.9B Schneider Electric supply-capacity reservation ahead of EVO construction on all five campuses.

(Low confidence) We assess a quiet executive-suite reorganization may be underway pre-IPO. Basis: President & CLO Thomas Morton — 17 years at the company and its long-time public voice — was last company-quoted in October 2025 and is absent from the March 2026-refreshed executive page with no announcement either way. Collection gap: no company statement; verify before relying on the org chart.

metrics.name: Take-private (Dec 2022)
metrics.actual: $34.25/share all-cash, ~$11B including debt — DigitalBridge and IFM Investors; announced May 11, 2022, closed December 6, 2022
metrics.result: Ends the 2017-2022 NYSE run (SWCH); debt financing led by TD Securities with SocGen, RBC, Citizens, Truist, Santander, Scotiabank and MUFG

metrics.name: Aware Super minority stake (Jul 2023)
metrics.actual: Australian pension fund Aware Super partnered with DigitalBridge to take an undisclosed minority stake

metrics.name: IPO exploration (Sep 2024)
metrics.actual: Reuters: owners exploring an IPO at ~$40B including debt, listing as early as 2025
metrics.result: First public valuation mark since the take-private — ~3.6x the 2022 deal in 21 months

metrics.name: IPO mandate (Jul 2026)
metrics.actual: Reuters: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan hired to lead an IPO raising up to $10B at up to $80B including debt, as soon as Q4 2026; prior private-round talks at $40B+
metrics.result: Would rank among the largest US listings of the AI cycle

metrics.name: Confidential filing (Aug 2026)
metrics.actual: Bloomberg: confidential S-1 filed; listing possible as soon as November; July Bloomberg reporting put the target near $50B including debt; BofA, Citi, Goldman, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley on the deal; a16z-led private round targeting ~$2B with Ben Horowitz expected to join the board
metrics.result: Company has not confirmed terms; valuation range across reports spans $40-80B including debt

periods.commentary: All valuation marks are press-attributed (Reuters/Bloomberg), not company-confirmed. Ownership split between DigitalBridge-managed vehicles (majority), IFM Investors and Aware Super is not publicly quantified.

metrics.name: ABS master trust
metrics.actual: Five issuances since 2024 totaling ~$4.2B, all secured green bonds, rated by Morningstar DBRS: $752M (Mar 2024), $940M (Jun 2024), $1.1B (Mar 2025 — largest green data-center ABS at issue), $659M (Oct 2025 — first dedicated to new development), $768M (Apr 2026; AAA/AA-low/A-low; Reno collateral ~1.4M sq ft, 52+MW)
metrics.result: Trust at Apr 2026: 11 data centers, five markets, 550+ customers, ~84% of revenue from investment-grade tenants; company claims largest single data-center ABS issuer since 2024

metrics.name: CMBS
metrics.actual: $2.4B single-asset single-borrower CMBS (Mar 2025) — largest green data-center CMBS ever, second-largest data-center CMBS in history; collateral Las Vegas 7, Las Vegas 9, Reno 2; 66 investors, seven tranches
metrics.result: With the concurrent $1.1B ABS, refinanced the majority of the remaining take-private acquisition debt

metrics.name: Bank facilities
metrics.actual: $4.25B sustainability-linked borrowing-base facility + $770M revolver (Sep 2024, 25+ banks, JPM/TD structuring) → expanded to $10B combined (Jul 2025) → corporate revolver upsized past $6B plus $3.5B performance LC facility for ~$10B combined liquidity (Jun 2026; TD/Wells Fargo and BBVA/Natixis leads)
metrics.result: 100% of 2022 take-private bank debt ($6.5B) retired by July 2025

metrics.name: Performance LC facility
metrics.actual: $2.6B syndicated performance letter-of-credit facility (Apr 2026) — industry first — backing utility performance assurance for new transmission and generation; upsized to $3.5B by June 2026
metrics.result: Cumulative capital raised since 2024: $20B by Jul 2025, $24B+ by Apr 2026 (company figures)

periods.commentary: The securitization disclosures are the only recurring public window into operating scale. No leverage, revenue or EBITDA figures have been published since the take-private.

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.actual: Q1 $164.6M / Q2 $168.2M / Q3 $174.5M (last reported quarter before the December 2022 close)
metrics.expected: FY2022 company guidance $660-674M (+13% YoY at midpoint)
metrics.result: Tracking to guidance when reporting ceased; no full-year figure was ever published

metrics.name: Adjusted EBITDA
metrics.expected: FY2022 company guidance $345-357M (~52.6% margin at midpoint)
metrics.result: Guidance was the company's own, not analyst consensus

periods.commentary: Collection gap: Switch has published no revenue, EBITDA, headcount or consolidated balance-sheet data since going private in December 2022 — the FY2022 rows are a historical anchor, and current scale must be triangulated from securitization disclosures, facility sizes and press-reported valuations. A second gap: no aggregate operational MW or utilization is disclosed for any campus; published MW figures are build-out targets.
